correctness.rationale: The linear exact HMC coupling gives diagonal expected squared cosine powers exactly for every initial pair and integer number of iid steps. For even integer frequencies \(m\ge2\), the weighted identity \(F(s)=m\sin^2s+\cos^2(ms)\) has derivative \(-2m\sin((m-1)s)\cos((m+1)s)\), a sole first-lobe minimum at \(\delta=\pi/[2(m+1)]\), and a strict global barrier outside the first lobe via monotonicity of \(\sin^2(u)/u\) on \(u\le\pi/4\). The integrated inequality is sharp and its equality locus classifies all optimizing probability laws. Odd m is simultaneous quarter-period. Finite verifier independently tests many instances but does not prove infinity.

value.rationale: Arbitrary iid HMC duration selection is motivated by resonance, and the two-mode integer-ratio Gaussian is a canonical minimally nontrivial design problem. The nontrivial global weighted trigonometric supporting inequality resolves the complete sharp mean-square iid minimax for every integer m, proves a genuine even/odd exact-sampling dichotomy, and identifies all minimizing distributions. This is not the known harmonic flow identity alone and is not a wall-clock, nonstationary or multivariate-spectrum claim.
